## Use in Wildfires

- Classification: `adapted` rendering/transfer/navigation code and OBJ/MTL/JSON resources, plus `verbatim` PNG resources.
- Adapted files: `OrbitVisualRules.java` ports station LEAVING/TRANSFER/ARRIVING visual semantics, NTM's cubic circular easing, shortest-turn `clerp`, route-angle formula, two-real-hour local satellite orbit, apparent-size calculation, Sun scale, `0.01..0.5` point/body LOD, and the common `sunBrightness=1-eclipseAmount` / star-visibility contract; its source flat-body phase approximation is replaced by exact rotated-cube silhouette coverage, while the project requirement keeps player `+Y` exactly perpendicular to the ecliptic. `NtmOrbitSkyRenderer.java` ports the six-face night atlas with its per-face transformed vertex/UV contract, eclipse/distance-dependent alpha, colored point pass, and photosphere/corona order. The old fixed-function untextured black star-mask is intentionally folded into a single standard-alpha photosphere pass because separate coplanar squares produce black rims and striped flicker on the Forge 1.20.1 shader path. `OrbitClientIllumination.java` resolves the same station-local contract from synchronized observation context for the 1.20.1 lightmap. `ReusableReturnCapsuleEntity`, `ReturnCapsuleState`, `ReturnCapsuleVisuals` and `ReturnCapsuleService` adapt the reusable `rp_pod_20` launch/landing/docking/undocking state boundaries, rider stickiness, cross-dimension vehicle reconstruction, door/airbrake/leg curves, four-nozzle exhaust and station fuel/docking contract from `EntityRideableRocket`, `RenderDropPod`, `CelestialTeleporter` and `TileEntityOrbitalStation`; Wildfires replaces NTM's modular rocket, navigation drive, hydrazine and legacy custom tanks with one Forge-water capsule, stable UUID/passenger evidence, exactly-once transaction tickets, bounded chunk tickets and deterministic recovery. Player transfer retains NTM's same-UUID reconstruction and destination-remount behavior, but the Forge 1.20.1 physical order is intentionally vehicle-first: the target Level receives the reconstructed capsule before the player Respawn/teleport, then the authoritative passenger is reattached. This ordering is adapted from the separately recorded VS: Genesis high-version teleporter and prevents AddEntity/SetPassengers from racing behind Respawn. A missing rider is only remounted in the same level for at most 60 ticks, while a rider already in another level trips a terminal recovery fuse and is never teleported again. Recovery now sends an exact ticket/capsule abort acknowledgement so the modern captured-frame receiving screen cannot outlive the stopped server transaction. Launch input now follows NTM's `AWAITING && rider.isJumping` immediate action: one press consumes a one-shot latch, release immediately permits the next press, and a stale held press cannot fire after destination remount. The docking contract uses NTM's exact `coreY + 1.5 - entityHeight` base anchor, approaches upward from below, commits a bidirectional core/entity UUID lock and undocks downward. Core/proxy blocks remain structural ownership records but do not collide with their managed capsule entity. `ReusableReturnCapsuleRenderer` applies the synchronized part transforms through Forge 1.20.1 vertex consumers and renders the recorded upstream model/texture assets.
- Station core, capsule and navigation-drive adaptation: Wildfires now distributes the upstream `docking_port.obj` and `rp_drop_pod.obj` meshes with only a Forge `usemtl` selector and license comment added, supplies new Forge MTL/JSON bindings, and distributes the upstream `docking_port.png`, `rp_drop_pod.png` and `votv_f.png` bytes as `station_id_tape.png`. `StationCoreRenderer` preserves the upstream authored docking-port scale; the authoritative `BlockOrbitalStation.getDimensions()` block contract is one bottom-centre core plus forty-nine structure proxies filling the complete `5x5x2` volume. The initial core is the immutable primary port while operator-placed cores are removable NTM-style secondary ports, each with persistent UUID lock ownership and a pre-launch reservation. It draws upstream `Port` once and reuses upstream `ArmZP` at four 90-degree rotations with the original pivot and 2.25-degree-per-tick clamp motion. `ReusableReturnCapsuleRenderer` loads the complete upstream pod mesh/skin through Forge 1.20.1; in orbit it follows `RenderDropPod`'s unconditional `renderAll`, while on a surface it draws `DropPod`, `Door`, `Legs`, and the one upstream `Airbrake0` mesh at four rotations, deliberately excluding `HeatShield` so the model's bottom nozzle is exposed. `ReusableReturnCapsuleItem` adapts NTM's station launcher deployment into an atomic bottom-port placement transaction and uses the entity's complete physical bounds for ordinary surface placement. Wildfires adapts `ItemVOTVdrive` into a real internal one-tape slot: an operator records a real bound station UUID/display name, swaps that `ItemStack` into the capsule, and every action resolves it afresh against current SavedData, permissions, current celestial surface binding, journey state and an available complete docking core. The alignment also ports NTM's pre-ignition door close, multiple ports, approach/undock clamp timing, four main-nozzle exhaust emitters, re-entry/ground particles, and the actually used upstream `rocketIgnition.ogg` and `rocketFlyLight.ogg` sounds. NTM `rocketStage.ogg` is not registered or distributed because this reusable-pod route has no staged-rocket sound call. UUIDs replace NTM's mutable orbit-grid coordinates; failed station mutations cannot silently clear a destination, double-drain water, remove an entity or leave stale occupancy.
- Verbatim resources: `night.png`, `kerbol.png`, `sunspike.png`, and `planet.png` from `assets/hbm/textures/misc/space/`; `docking_port.png`, `rp_drop_pod.png`, the renamed `votv_f.png` navigation-tape icon, and `particle_base.png` used by the exact six-quad `ParticleExSmoke` presentation from their exact upstream paths listed in `files.csv`.
- Wildfires modifications: replaces NTM's solar-system registry with `CelestialState/CelestialBodyState`; converts the geocentric Wildfires ephemeris to heliocentric positions before applying NTM's route-angle formula; keeps Wildfires real radii instead of NTM's 3000 km render cap; monotonically compresses astronomical draw depth while preserving angular size so overlap uses correct near/far ordering; replaces fixed-function OpenGL/Tessellator calls with `RenderSystem`, `VertexBuffer` and Forge shaders; maps NTM station phases to synchronized Wildfires journey phases and rotates the complete sky presentation as one frame. A further adaptation replaces the unsafe world-space linear cruise chord with a cubic outward/lateral transfer arc between the two NTM-style local-orbit endpoints. Its clearance grows with both local orbit/body radius and route length, and full-path cube-exclusion sampling verifies that a target hidden behind the departure planet never makes the station presentation cross either endpoint cube. NTM's explicit parent/moon and shared-parent transfer categories are retained through the shared Wildfires `StationTransferTopology`: planet-orbit to child-moon, child-moon to planet and sibling-moon routes are conventional local transfers. Their visual transfer is planned in the moving common-primary frame: departure is reconstructed and locked at cruise start, the destination is predicted at cruise end from the synchronized TFC calendar rate, and the Moon prediction re-evaluates the same unified solar-longitude/synodic/inclination/node model used by the authoritative sky instead of rotating it around a spin-axis approximation. Each endpoint uses a bounded three-dimensional phasing-point search and a local safe-orbit gate. The central leg is a bounded common-primary cubic transfer orbit whose controls scale from the endpoint orbital radii and route chord; candidates first remain near the endpoint orbital chord plane, expand deterministically around square-body obstacles, and use ecliptic-normal detours only as a finite fallback. Candidate clearance now samples the complete five-leg path against every shared-primary moon at its matching journey time, with 96 to 512 adaptive samples based on the fastest child orbit, so a moon crossing the route between departure and arrival snapshots cannot be missed. The selected route is retained in a 24-entry bounded LRU keyed by station, celestial generation, endpoints, cruise epoch, duration and synchronized calendar rate; sky and lightmap reuse the same plan without per-frame replanning. Local heading is locked to that plan rather than the live moving target, and a delayed stale CRUISE snapshot hands off directly to the target's live stable orbit once its authoritative end time has passed. This replaces the former high-Z corridor above the complete satellite system. Segment progress is distributed by sampled physical path length and eased only at the full cruise endpoints, so internal gates retain non-zero through-speed. Cross-primary routes continue to use the interplanetary Bezier adaptation. Relativistic jump departure searches the source orbit for the first direct target line that clears every non-target conservative cube bound, falling back to the same safe interplanetary arc only if an entire source orbit remains blocked. During that search the complete sky now follows one fixed-endpoint quaternion path from the inertial station attitude to the acceleration-start direct target heading; the ordinary NTM planar route yaw is not layered onto jump departure, and the lock endpoint is not recomputed from the moving phasing observer. After lock, Wildfires independently adds a distance-scaled straight visual flight: the integrated 3-second acceleration reaches a route-specific cruise speed and all 8 cruise seconds move linearly; the 3-second deceleration analytically reaches the non-zero world speed required by the following ten-tick target reveal rather than stopping at the phase boundary. The target remains an NTM-style point through deceleration; the first 10 arrival ticks continue from that exact speed to the target-facing stable orbit while blending to normal body LOD, then a target-centred spherical arc performs ordinary orbital adjustment. Full three-dimensional target lock uses a fixed ecliptic-north roll reference rather than an underdetermined opposite-vector rotation, avoiding mid-turn orientation flips. The NTM night cubemap mesh remains rigid during a jump: an independent Wildfires shader inverse-maps the visually capped aberrated direction to the exact six NTM atlas faces so stars slide across the box rather than folding its geometry. Narrow edge bands continuously blend adjacent face samples while Doppler/exposure depends only on the observed angular distance from the forward centre, so atlas faces cannot create brightness seams. The opaque black vacuum pass is reusable when synchronized station/celestial context is temporarily unavailable, preventing the orbit clear colour from showing through; star-atlas sampling stays half a real face texel inside each 768-pixel NTM cell so cross-edge motion cannot bleed from a non-neighboring atlas cell. `OrbitClientIllumination` consumes the same calendar-rate- and month-length-aware frame so visible planet occlusion and the orbit lightmap cannot disagree during accelerated TFC time or a frozen visual debug clock.
- Local-transfer correction: ordinary non-lunar satellites convert TFC calendar displacement through the current `daysInMonth * 12` year length into the same astronomical-day scale used by the unified 17-body ephemeris, and use the synchronized configured orbit-plane normal. The bounded 24-entry LRU identity now includes the absolute departure calendar tick, month length, synchronized rate and complete synchronized celestial settings snapshot in addition to station/generation/endpoints/cruise epoch. A repeated route therefore cannot reuse an earlier moon intercept, and Titan, Triton, Charon plus every Galilean transfer track the authoritative moving orbit.
- Jump-arrival continuity correction: when a synchronized client still holds a just-finished `JUMP_DECELERATING` snapshot, its already-authoritative end timestamp is sufficient to extrapolate only the fixed first ten ARRIVING ticks. This keeps target size, observer displacement, background motion and target lock on the same curve as the eventual server snapshot without changing server state or packet data. Procedural target atlases are also resolved during direction search/acceleration rather than synchronously inside the ten-tick reveal.
- Jump-orbit orientation correction: after the ten-tick target reveal, observer displacement retains the target-centred spherical arrival arc, while the complete sky unlocks along one quaternion path between the fixed jump heading and the final inertial station attitude. It deliberately does not restore NTM's planar route yaw while also following a changing live-target lock endpoint, because that two-endpoint blend can switch the quaternion shortest-arc branch and rotate the sky by nearly 180 degrees in one frame.
- Relativistic timing refinement: the independent Wildfires ray-presentation layer now joins the fixed three-second acceleration, eight-second cruise and three-second release with first-derivative-continuous contraction curves. Cruise spends four seconds smoothly reducing the contraction rate and four more seconds continuing at one-third of the initial rate, reaching a finite `0.93` visual-aberration endpoint below the shared Java/GLSL `0.94` point-collapse guard. The acceleration trail follows the analytic contraction rate through its three-second boundary, then its short residual retracts monotonically to zero during only the first cruise second; the final three-second release keeps its independent signed window unchanged. Twelve fixed seamless atlas samples run only while either strength is active, so the remaining seven cruise seconds and arrival use no trail samples. This changes neither the NTM-derived phase semantics nor the distance-scaled observer motion, target lock, Doppler beta or following ten-tick arrival geometry. `RelativisticVisualRules.java` and the shader formulas remain outside `files.csv` because they are independently authored from the user-supplied special-relativity reference rather than adapted from an NTM file; the adapted `NtmOrbitSkyRenderer` row records only the uniform handoff and its current hash.
- Lossless frame-cost refinement: the adapted orbit rules now construct one direct-jump `JumpLine` per complete visual frame and reuse it for observer displacement and fixed target heading. The unchanged 720-orbit/720-fallback search preprocesses every non-target obstacle into primitive coordinate/radius arrays, then evaluates the same ordered segment projection, square root and conservative-radius comparison without per-candidate vector allocation. A separate Wildfires-authored `OrbitVisualFrameCache` shares only a byte-for-byte-equivalent immutable frame when context/state identities and all time/rate/month inputs match exactly; its fixed factory also avoids capture allocation on cache hits, and it is intentionally outside `files.csv`. The independent `OrbitSkyRenderer` coordination layer also skips depth-buffer clears after point and Sun passes that have depth writes disabled, while preserving the clear after every successfully rendered solid cube. These changes do not alter NTM phase semantics, candidate/sample counts, sky/body ordering, trajectory, timing, Doppler/exposure values or rendered pixels.
- Lossless NTM OBJ submission refinement (2026-08-14): the adapted station/capsule renderers retain the exact upstream mesh, component count, material, light, overlay, Pose/normal matrices and vertex order while entering an explicit Wildfires component-selection scope. A separately authored `NtmObjFastRenderer` and Forge-private Mesh Mixin replace Forge's allocation-heavy `putBulkData` only when the selected mesh receives the exact vanilla `BufferBuilder` runtime class. Its identity cache flattens the unchanged 32-int BakedQuad payload once, then executes the same JOML transforms, RGBA/UV/light/normal rules and `NEW_ENTITY` vertex writes; wrappers, custom consumers, malformed quads and the complete orbit capsule fall back untouched. Randomized final-buffer tests compare every output byte against Forge, and resource reload clears both model and primitive identities. The helper, scope and Forge Mixin are Wildfires-authored performance infrastructure and remain outside `files.csv`; only the three adapted coordination files carry updated hashes.
- Shader-binding cost refinement (2026-08-14): `NtmOrbitSkyRenderer` now consumes a resource-generation-bound `RelativisticSkyShader.Bindings` object rather than repeating three named uniform lookups in every active relativistic frame. The dual-derived `NtmAscentPlanetRenderer` likewise consumes the Genesis texture/atmosphere binding objects described in the Genesis record. Uniform write order and values, NTM atlas, altitude curve, cubemap passes, particles, transfer states and rendered pixels are unchanged; each shader reload constructs a new immutable binding set for its new `ShaderInstance`.
- Return-capsule transfer refinement (2026-08-14): the adapted Forge 1.20.1 implementation retains NTM's same-UUID/same-NBT vehicle reconstruction and destination remount contract while changing only the high-version entity ordering to VS: Genesis' vehicle-first pattern: create and `addDuringTeleport` the target capsule, remove the source instance, teleport the player, then `startRiding` the already tracked target vehicle. Explicit source-client pre-arm, target tracking, server-confirmation, rendered-target-ready and commit acknowledgements remain required by modern dimension packets. The source remains frozen and mounted in `PREPARED` until the client thread captures the flight frame and proves the exact ticket/capsule pair; only the persisted `CLIENT_ARMED` stage permits transfer. At the target, the authoritative `ClientboundSetPassengersPacket` is retransmitted every five ticks through both remount stages. The client also searches only the exact target dimension and capsule UUID, locally repairs that passenger graph only when the player is not riding another entity, and clears velocity/fall distance until the server graph and two rendered target frames agree. Launch, docking, undocking and landing use the upstream altitude/`rocketVelocity`/20-tick port-wait/±0.1-block-per-tick contracts instead of fixed Wildfires interpolation. A bounded one-chunk flight ticket is handed forward immediately after pitched ascent movement so an unobserved capsule cannot unload at a chunk boundary; it is released at transfer, commit or recovery. The physical jump key is sampled across the short respawn window without manufacturing a release/press pair. These compatibility additions do not replace the NTM behavior contract and remain part of the listed LGPL-adapted capsule files.
- Return-capsule client-passenger refinement (2026-08-14): NTM's moving-state `canExitCapsule` protection remains authoritative on the Forge 1.20.1 server, but is no longer allowed to cancel the client-side temporary dismount used by `ClientPacketListener.handleSetEntityPassengersPacket`. That vanilla handler must eject the pre-Respawn passenger graph before attaching the replacement `LocalPlayer`; applying the server rule on both physical sides prevented the repeatedly transmitted destination graph from converging. Forge 1.20.1 also calls the target vehicle's `couldAcceptPassenger()` even for forced `startRiding(..., true)`; because the reconstructed ticket is authoritative server-only state, the client target capsule now accepts the authoritative passenger graph without consulting that unsynchronized ticket, while the server retains the complete state/ticket gate. The target barrier requires both object identity with the exact currently tracked target capsule and a reciprocal passenger-list link, while a removed or wrong-level same-UUID capsule may be detached as a bounded Respawn repair. Unrelated live vehicles remain untouched. This changes only the high-version synchronization adaptation and preserves NTM's server-side no-exit, same-UUID remount and flight behavior.
- Return-capsule orbit-scene barrier refinement (2026-08-14): before the target vehicle/player Respawn sequence, the server now sends the authoritative station observation context for the same ticket. Surface destinations still require two ordinary destination render passes, but an orbit destination requires two consecutive passes in which the exact passenger graph is confirmed and the current celestial body's Genesis square surface was actually drawn. A missing context, missing celestial state, point-only LOD, unavailable shader or black NTM vacuum fallback resets the frame count instead of releasing the capsule early. Bounded transition-stage/readiness logs are emitted only when state bits change, preserving the NTM flight and docking contract while making the modern transfer barrier diagnosable.
- Return-capsule high-atmosphere refinement (2026-08-14): `NtmAscentAtmosphereVisuals` ports `SkyProviderCelestial`'s exact `clamp((800-Y)/500,0,1)` surface-sky curvature from Y=300 through Y=800 and its clamped `(Y-200)/300` underfoot-body reveal. Wildfires synchronizes the active ticket's body ID, requires that body's datapack definition to bind the capsule's current existing dimension, and submits the body through a full-dimension `AFTER_SKY` pass. `NtmAscentPlanetRenderer` replaces NTM's flat body-texture quad with the separately recorded Genesis mesh, cubemap, rigid cloud shell and atmosphere; texture selection, axial rotation and centre-star incoming light are body-driven rather than hard-coded to Earth. A bound surface dimension's registered celestial provider remains authoritative; when none exists, only this ascent pass reuses the cached common-universe ephemeris. Incoming light is resolved from the Sun to the ticket's actual ephemeris body, so a Mars/Moon/other bound-body ascent cannot inherit Earth's light vector. The built-in data still binds only Earth to `minecraft:overworld`, and Y>900 still transfers exclusively into `wildfires:orbit`.
- Return-capsule physical/presentation refinement (2026-08-14): the dedicated Forge entity now restores `EntityRideableRocket`'s logical width `2`, `rp_pod_20` height `3 + 1 = 4`, mounted offset `4 - 2.5 = 1.5`, and resulting `coreY + 1.5 - 4` bottom-port anchor instead of reusing the narrower OBJ visible bounds as collision dimensions. Surface arrival starts at the exact upstream Y=800 and re-queries live terrain height on every landing tick. The entity renderer preserves `RenderRocketCustom`'s `Y(yaw-90) -> Z(pitch) -> Y(90-yaw)` attitude conjugation. Dock clamps again keep their own client `prevRot/rot` state and move by 2.25 degrees per tick solely from the synchronized occupied-port UUID, rather than deriving arm position from a nearby entity's phase. The light-flight loop restores the upstream 1.0 volume. These changes retain the exact recorded OBJ/PNG resources, Wildfires square-planet presentation and the modern reliable-transfer barrier.
- Return-capsule scale, speed and ground-effect refinement (2026-08-14): `StationCoreRenderer` now follows `RenderOrbitalStation` at the authored OBJ scale and `(x + 0.5, y + 1, z + 0.5)` anchor; the logical proxy volume does not shrink the visible five-unit port. The separate Forge item model converts NTM `ItemRenderBase`'s inventory transform to a `0.125` GUI scale without changing the world model. Approach, undocking and landing execute exactly one upstream `+0.1`, `-0.1` or terrain-distance step per server tick; the rejected four-substep time compression is absent. Because Forge tracks this entity every tick, the client moving state converges to each authoritative tracker target in one client tick instead of spreading an already per-tick NTM movement across vanilla's later two-to-four ticks; ordinary previous/current partial-tick rendering remains active and no client-side second movement is predicted. The upstream `rocketVelocity` is synchronized explicitly for airbrakes, terminal ignition and particles. Near-ground launch/landing shock smoke uses the live height and original `groundHeight + 0.5` centre.
- Dock-ownership refinement (2026-08-14): NTM's `TileEntityOrbitalStation` holds a live docked rocket reference, so a removed rocket cannot leave a usable port permanently occupied. The Forge persistent UUID adaptation now reconciles bidirectional locks immediately at the surface-launch action boundary: only a station-owned capsule with a valid upward transition ticket or a physically present, exactly docked stable entity may retain the port. An orphaned UUID from an older save is released before the complete-port selection, while a damaged `5x5x2` shell still rejects launch without reserving water or creating a ticket.
- Return-capsule particle refinement (2026-08-14): `ParticleExSmoke` now submits the original six independently grey/scale/Gaussian-offset quads from one fixed per-particle render seed, uses the verbatim `particle_base.png`, fades over 100..139 ticks and applies the original 0.76 damping before movement. `ExplosionLarge.spawnShock`/client shock mode again emits only 1..3 particle states at the complete `1 + Gaussian` radial strength with an integer-radian initial turn and equal angular spacing; six entity billboards no longer substitute for one six-quad particle. `ParticleGasFlame` restores the inherited 1.7.10 `EntityFX/EntitySmokeFX` seed motion, 0.96 base damping, current-frame +0.004 Y displacement, subsequent +0.005 Y velocity, additional 0.75 X/Z damping, reverse 7-to-0 smoke animation, HSB quantization, fullbright, and the old 6.5×0.1 = 0.65 rendered scale.
- Return-capsule visible-final-approach and particle-delivery refinement (2026-08-15): the modern target-scene barrier has already loaded the exact station, passenger graph and Genesis body before flight is released, so the capsule now enters the visible docking leg 24 blocks below the real port instead of repeating NTM's legacy dedicated-orbit-world climb from Y=0 to its Y=127 station. The upstream 20-tick port wait, one `+0.1` movement per server tick, `coreY + 1.5 - capsuleHeight` anchor and bidirectional lock remain unchanged. NTM adds both `ParticleGasFlame` and `ParticleExSmoke` directly to the client `EffectRenderer`; the Forge adaptation now uses the equivalent forced always-visible submission so modern particle-status/distance gates cannot discard an exhaust or ground-shock state before its registered provider creates it. The six-quad geometry, 1..3 count, velocity, texture, lifetime, damping, colour and scale are unchanged; one bounded first-creation log per provider supplies real-client evidence without per-particle logging.
- Ascent-shell and station-core interaction refinement (2026-08-15): the bound-surface renderer retains NTM's altitude progression but computes the rotated Genesis cube body's true outward ray distance including its cloud and atmosphere shells, so the body is not submitted while the camera remains inside the outer shell. Vanilla/TFC local clouds are cancelled only after that same strict departure boundary; the planet's Genesis orbital cloud shell remains part of the distant body. NTM's exact `5x5x2` core dimensions are now fully materialized as one root plus forty-nine proxies. The top-centre proxy adapts `BlockOrbitalStation`/`TileEntityOrbitalStation` activation for boarding, tape swap and safe dismount, while `StationCoreOverlay` adapts the upstream look-overlay information contract. Core Forge-water input forwards only to the physically present, bidirectionally locked pod at that port. Proxy ownership, teardown and recovery are resolved only at placement, interaction, destruction and server-start boundaries; there is no periodic orphan scan or cleanup tick.
- Return-capsule surface-landing refinement (2026-08-14): the adapted `LANDING` loop now preserves NTM's occupied-descent-column response by shifting the recorded surface endpoint along exactly one random X or Z axis by `-5/+5`, then carrying the same endpoint into the internal home position and modern chunk-ticket ledger. Contact with any liquid enters the persistent `TIPPING` state and applies the upstream `(stateTimer * 0.1)^2` pitch curve capped at 90 degrees; lava retains the upstream delayed capsule/tape drop and strength-5 explosion at 95 ticks. Ordinary collision always reaches the visible 45-tick `LANDED` door-open sequence even when the modern internal station tape remains installed. One fresh jump edge then only reactivates that tape and closes the door; a release and second edge are required for ignition, preventing the same held input from launching the reverse trip.
- Return-capsule input-edge refinement (2026-08-14): normal mounted gameplay again sources NTM's `rider.isJumping` action from Forge's movement-input update edge, while physical-key polling is retained only across the modern captured-frame receiving screen where ordinary movement input can pause. Both routes share one client edge latch. The server packet now enters `ReturnCapsuleService.handlePrimaryActionInput` once, atomically records the press/release state and performs at most one close/launch/undock action; release only rearms the next edge. This preserves NTM's immediate waiting-state jump while retaining the modern rule that one held key cannot become a reverse launch after dimension remount.
- Return-capsule passenger-pose refinement (2026-08-14): NTM `EntityRideableRocket.updateRiderPosition` moves the passenger along the pitched rocket axis but does not rotate the living model, so a modern third-person player remains world-upright and clips through the reusable pod. `ReturnCapsulePassengerPose` now makes the pod renderer and passenger renderer share the exact recorded `RenderRocketCustom` `Y(yaw-90) -> Z(pitch) -> Y(90-yaw)` conjugation. A client-only `LivingEntityRenderer` injection applies it after the renderer's own pose push and immediately before vanilla body-yaw setup, only when the living entity actually rides the Wildfires reusable capsule. Player-local yaw/animation, camera input, service-side orientation, collisions and the NTM seat trajectory remain unchanged.
- Return-capsule final motion, camera, docking and service-port refinement (2026-08-15): the surface ascent pass now suppresses the still-loaded flat local chunk layers and Minecraft/TFC cloud deck only after the camera has crossed the rotated Genesis square body's outermost rendered shell, while retaining the square body, rigid orbital cloud shell and atmosphere. The NTM `-0.1` undocking motion remains visible for twenty-four blocks below the real port before the already-preloaded transfer barrier takes over; surface descent preserves the upstream distance curve but snaps the final `0.25` block collision tail to the live terrain height so modern swept collision cannot spend many seconds at the `-0.005` minimum. The passenger seat is lowered by `0.5` block, and `ReturnCapsuleCameraMixin` applies the same recorded `RenderRocketCustom` attitude quaternion to the first-person camera position, basis and near plane that `ReturnCapsulePassengerPose` uses for the living model. Reservation and true docking UUIDs are separate: a reserved port keeps its four clamps open, exact physical docking closes them, and undocking releases the true lock before movement. The twelve NTM connection positions are represented by no-tick `StationFluidPortBlockEntity` proxies that cache the root core position and forward Forge water only to the physically present, bidirectionally locked capsule. NTM shock smoke's caller height `groundHeight + 0.5` and its internal additional `+0.5` are preserved as the final visible `groundHeight + 1.0` emission height. Capsule recovery drops the internal navigation tape separately from the fuel-bearing capsule item. Moving chunk tickets are owned by the exact per-trip UUID and remove only that same UUID, never a co-located player's ticket or another capsule's ticket.
- Return-capsule body-relative flight and client-ground refinement (2026-08-15): direct review of the complete NTM inheritance chain established that `EntityRideableRocket` overrides `EntityThrowableNT.motionMult()` to `4` in every moving state. Wildfires now retains the upstream `rocketVelocity` values but integrates launch, docking, undocking and terrain-distance landing through the same fourfold displacement, correcting the previous one-quarter-speed final two blocks and 24-block station corridors. The final `0.25`-block modern collision snap remains only an epsilon terminator. `CelestialTransferProfile` generalizes NTM's absolute surface Y=200/300/500/800/900 assumptions to an altitude above the authoritative landing top, with bounded scaling from synchronized body diameter and the datapack atmosphere radius/density; the same curve runs forward during ascent and backward during re-entry for any explicitly bound non-star body. The capsule synchronizes that landing-top Y separately because a newly transferred Forge client may temporarily report `minBuildHeight` from an unapplied heightmap even while terrain is visible; shock smoke therefore remains at the true NTM `ground+1` point. After square-body reveal the local flat terrain, clouds, rain/snow draw and rain particle/sound tick are all suppressed while the Genesis body/cloud/atmosphere remain; every one of those local-scene gates now consumes the same landing-top-relative and body-size-aware reveal boundary rather than an absolute world Y. Camera attitude is first-person only: a detached vanilla camera keeps its completed collision clamp instead of being rotated into fresh exhaust billboards. The pod uses the culled exterior render type matching the upstream outside shell, so exterior backfaces no longer fill the cockpit view. These changes add no dimension or surface binding; the built-in set still binds only Earth to `minecraft:overworld`.
- Return-capsule player-occupancy refinement (2026-08-17): the Forge adaptation now accepts only `Player` passengers in the capsule's sole seat. Surface-ascent sky/body/local-weather gates additionally require the active camera observer itself to be that directly seated player; an unbound login-frame camera, non-player observer or detached player resolves to no ascent scene. Ignition, light-flight audio and forced exhaust/ground particles require a reciprocal direct player/capsule passenger link, so a state-only or empty capsule cannot emit launch effects. The authoritative server launch action already required the exact `ServerPlayer` as both direct vehicle rider and first passenger; this refinement closes the generic entity-capacity and client-presentation paths without changing NTM altitude, motion, state, sound or particle curves for a valid player flight.
- Surface-transition satellite-shadow continuity (2026-08-15): the reusable-capsule underfoot cube now consumes the same bounded four-caster ephemeris frame as the ordinary orbit renderer instead of clearing all satellite-shadow uniforms. Caster centres and half-sizes remain normalized by the receiving body's synchronized physical radius, so body-size changes preserve the correct geometric scale; the same finite-square-star umbra/penumbra pass is submitted to the square surface, rigid cloud shell and atmosphere shell without a shadow texture or framebuffer.
- Return-capsule high-altitude interpolation and render-state refinement (2026-08-15): direct review of `EntityThrowableInterp` confirmed that each tracker update retains the supplied interpolation count (normally three) instead of snapping in one client tick. The Forge entity now preserves that count, while the capsule, NTM axial seat, third-person passenger and first-person camera all consume one interpolated vehicle-frame anchor. The dual-derived square-body `AFTER_SKY` pass also restores depth testing, depth writes and back-face culling before chunks/entities render; this prevents the pod shell, four repeated `Airbrake0` meshes and passenger geometry from drawing through one another during both ascent and re-entry. The server-side NTM fourfold motion integration, square-planet pixels and transfer timing are unchanged.
- Return-capsule third-person dispatcher anchoring refinement (2026-08-15): Forge 1.20.1 uses `xo/yo/zo` for `Camera.setup` but the distinct `xOld/yOld/zOld` frame in `LevelRenderer.renderEntity`. The rigid NTM seat helper now exposes both domains explicitly. `PlayerRenderer.getRenderOffset` binds the complete player render, layers and Forge player events to the capsule's renderer-domain seat before drawing, while the living renderer applies only the shared NTM attitude. A narrowly scoped `EntityRenderer.shouldRender` gate keeps a true capsule passenger visible with its tracked vehicle so the old passenger AABB cannot make the corrected model flicker at the frustum boundary. Server passenger physics, capsule interpolation, fourfold motion and Genesis rendering remain unchanged.
- Return-capsule detached-camera anchoring refinement (2026-08-15): the previous dispatcher correction bound the third-person player model but left `Camera.setup` centred on the passenger's separate `xo/yo/zo` history, allowing the capsule drawn from `xOld/yOld/zOld` to surge and rebound relative to the view. `ReturnCapsuleCameraMixin` now translates only the detached camera centre to the exact renderer-domain NTM seat immediately before vanilla `Camera#getMaxZoom` casts its collision rays. Vanilla player look, front/rear selection, collision distance and completed zoom remain authoritative, and the reusable-pod attitude quaternion is still first-person-only so a detached camera cannot be rotated into the shell or exhaust. This is a Forge 1.20.1 interpolation-domain adaptation of NTM's rigid `updateRiderPosition` contract; server motion, passenger physics, Genesis rendering and transfer state are unchanged.
- Ordinary inter-system ingress refinement (2026-08-16): NTM `SolarSystem#getDeltaVBetween` explicitly climbs the celestial parent tree for moon-to-other-system transfers, while its visual `calculateMetricsBetweenSatelliteOrbits` still uses the source comment's provisional straight lerp. Wildfires now carries the hierarchical intent into `OrbitVisualRules`: an ordinary cross-system cruise locks its departure and end-of-cruise intercept in a Sun-following frame, treats the target planet and every moving satellite as a time-matched obstacle, reaches a target-primary-following gate outside the outermost satellite orbit, and completes capture in that moving primary frame. Both this planner and the existing common-primary planner test the swept relative segment between adjacent 96..512 ephemeris samples against each rotating cube's conservative bounding sphere instead of testing sample points alone. The locked NTM-style travel heading, 24-entry cache, stable-orbit endpoints and delayed-phase handoff remain deterministic; jump travel, server journey state, destination authority, dimensions and surface bindings are unchanged.
- Ordinary inter-system endpoint-capture correction (2026-08-16): adverse-phase regression reproduced an inward-side Earth-to-Callisto approach crossing Callisto itself and a high-calendar-rate Earth-to-Europa approach crossing the live moon between parent-frame samples. Cross-system departure now uses the station radius around the source body rather than the source body's radius from its parent. After the target-system ingress gate, the route follows the live authoritative target body, phases on an outer target-centred sphere, descends along one target-centred ray to a conservative safe gate, and completes a spherical stable-orbit adjustment; an inward-side station endpoint therefore cannot turn the final leg into a chord through either the target moon or its parent. The target anchor blends from the planned Sun-frame gate to the live ephemeris only while still on the outer sphere, retaining sub-tick continuity. Inter-system prediction now samples at least once per server tick with a bounded 2048-sample fast-moon ceiling, expands failed system-gate candidates through eleven deterministic scales, and rejects every plan whose final relative-motion sweep is not strictly positive instead of returning the least-negative collision. Pure regression covers every built-in satellite as an adverse arrival and departure endpoint, all moving bodies, the existing 1200x Jupiter/Europa cases, final authoritative interception and locked heading. This remains an LGPL-3.0-only modification of the listed adapted file; normal/jump authority, dimensions, surface bindings, propulsion and journey timing are unchanged.
- Partition: every adapted/verbatim Java, OBJ, MTL, JSON, PNG and OGG destination listed in `files.csv` is LGPL-3.0-only. The listed station-core classes are included because their multi-port reservation, dock membership and animated-clamp lifecycle now directly adapt `OrbitalStation` / `TileEntityOrbitalStation`; unrelated Wildfires station SavedData and ephemeris code outside that list retain their separately stated licenses unless otherwise listed by another partition.
- Corresponding source/relinking: the complete adapted Java source, resource files and build scripts are provided in this repository. The root ARR notice excludes this LGPL partition and does not restrict modification or reverse engineering of it. Recipients can replace/modify the listed sources and rebuild the combined JAR.

- Notice completion (2026-10-16): all forty adapted Java destinations now carry the `LGPL-3.0-only` notice with the upstream class each one adapts and a summary of what Wildfires changed. Six station-core classes (`StationCoreBlock`, `StationCoreBlockEntity`, `StationCoreService`, `StationDockCoreItem`, `StationStructureBlock`, `StationServerEvents`) had previously carried no notice at all; only comments were added, and no statement, field, method body or behavior changed.
